parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Hello, Creative Center.

Hello there. I’m phoning to book a place on your next two-day drama workshop.

Okay, let me just check. Yes, we’ve still got room on that course.

Great.

Can I have your full name?

Yes, it’s Jan Creswick. That’s C-R-E-S-W-I-C-K.

Thanks Jan. And are you coming on your own?

Yes.

And have you done any of our courses before?

Yes, I did one a couple of years ago.

Great. So you may be on our computer records. Which course did you do?

The "Writing for the Theatre" course.

Okay. Right. Yes, here we are. Oh, so that’s 20 Gregory Avenue.

Uh, Gregory Place, actually.

Okay. I’ll correct that on the computer. And can I ask if you work?

Yes, I want to be an actor, but I’m working as a waitress at the moment.

After this course, who knows? Right, back to the paperwork. So we’re enrolling you on the two-day course that starts tomorrow, the 30th of May.

Oh, sorry, no. On the 13th of June. I meant the one starting in two weeks. Is that still all right?

Oh, that’s fine.

Can you tell me something about accommodation?

Yes. People usually come the evening before the course starts. The cost of the course includes accommodation for two nights.

Well, I’ll make sure I’m there in good time so I can meet the others that evening and settle in. Is 5:30 too early to arrive?

No, that’s fine. And you’ll finish no later than five o’clock on the last day.

Right.

Okay. Right. Just a few other things. Any dietary information we should know? All the food is provided and we use organic produce as often as we can.

Oh, that sounds great. But I don’t eat anything that’s made from milk. I know that can be difficult.

Oh, it’s not a problem. What about meat? Do you eat that?

I don’t eat much of it, but that’s fine. You don’t need to note that.

Sure?

Yes. Hey, I am really looking forward to this.

Great. I don’t know if you know this, but we may divide into two groups in the afternoon if we have more than 16 people on the course. If we do that, there’ll be a choice of doing comic or what we call classic work.

Oh, I’d always go with comedy. I’m much more interested in that.

Now, how did you find out about this course? Was it the adverts in the Sunday newspaper?

No. In fact, I looked for drama courses on the internet and I saw that you were doing one. When I read about it, I just thought, "Hey, why not?"

Okay.

I saw that you send out some pre-course material.

Yes.

I don’t have much time to read any of the books you’re recommending, but I’d be grateful for your leaflet—the one you mentioned in your publicity?

Sure. I’ll put a copy in the post to you.

Thanks a lot. I can’t wait.

Wait till you see what we have in store!

analyses.content: 姓名拼写是 Part 1 的必拿分。听到 "Can I have your full name?" 就要准备好记录接下来的每一个字母。
Can I have your full name? Yes, it’s Jan Creswick. That’s C-R-E-S-W-I-C-K。
Jan 报出姓名后，为了确保工作人员准确记录，主动拼写了自己的姓氏 Creswick。
So you may be on our computer records. Which course did you do? The "Writing for the Theatre" course。
听到 "Which course did you do?" 这种问句时，后面跟着的专有名词就是答案。拼写时英美式均可（-re 或 -er）。
工作人员在查询旧记录时，Jan 确认她几年前参加过的课程是“戏剧写作”。
Oh, so that’s 20 Gregory Avenue. Uh, Gregory Place, actually. Okay. I’ll correct that on the computer。
听到地址时，重点防范工作人员读出的“旧信息”。凡是听到 Actually 或者 Oh, sorry 这种转折词，后面的才是真地址。
工作人员读出电脑里旧的地址后缀 Avenue，被 Jan 纠正为 Place。
And can I ask if you work? Yes, I want to be an actor, but I’m working as a waitress at the moment。
卷面问的是 Current occupation（当前职业）。雅思常考“理想”与“现实”的区分，want to be 后面的职业通常是干扰项。
Jan 表示她虽然想当演员（actor），但目前实际维持生计的职业是 waitress。
So we’re enrolling you on the two-day course that starts tomorrow, the 30th of May. Oh, sorry, no. On the 13th of June. I meant the one starting in two weeks。
月份和日期辨析是重灾区。必须排除工作人员主动提出的 30th of May，这是典型的先导干扰。
工作人员以为是明天的课（30th of May），Jan 立刻纠正说是两周后即 13th of June 开始的那一期。
Jan 确认了她计划到达（arrival）的时间是下午 5:30。
录音中明确提到了晚上到达（evening），所以这个答案是需要加 pm 的，不能不加。
Well, I’ll make sure I’m there in good time so I can meet the others that evening and settle in. Is 5:30 too early to arrive? No, that’s fine。
All the food is provided and we use organic produce as often as we can. Oh, that sounds great. But I don’t eat anything that’s made from milk。
听到 dietary information 就要立刻警觉。虽然她随后也讨论了 meat，但明确说“不需要记（don't need to note that）”，所以答案不选 meat。
关于饮食限制，Jan 强调她不吃任何含有 milk 成分的食物。
If we do that, there’ll be a choice of doing comic or what we call classic work. Oh, I’d always go with comedy. I’m much more interested in that。
录音中提到了 comic（形容词）和 classic 两个选项，Jan 确定了前者。填入名词 comedy 最符合语法习惯。
工作人员给出下午课程的两个选择，Jan 明确表示她对 comedy（喜剧）更感兴趣。
Was it the adverts in the Sunday newspaper? No. In fact, I looked for drama courses on the internet and I saw that you were doing one。
还是典型的干扰排除。工作人员问是不是看到报纸（newspaper）广告，Jan 明确回答 No 之后引出了正确途径。
Jan 解释说她是在 internet 上搜索课程时发现的，而不是通过报纸。
I don’t have much time to read any of the books you’re recommending, but I’d be grateful for your leaflet—the one you mentioned in your publicity?
听到 books 不要动笔，Jan 的态度是 don't have much time（没空看），只有对 leaflet 的态度是 grateful（想要）。
Jan 表示没时间看书（books），她只需要一份宣传广告里提到的 leaflet（传单）。
